rounds.proof_sketch: eps change from 1e-5 to 9.9e-6 causes max relative change in inv_std of 0.5% (when variance=0). For any normalized output y: |diff| ≈ 0.005*|y| which is always < 0.01 + 0.01*|y| = atol + rtol*|ref|. The 0.5% relative error is smaller than the 1% rtol threshold.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation reduces epsilon by 1%, which causes at most a 0.5% relative change in the inverse standard deviation (1/sqrt(var+eps)). This maximum occurs when variance is zero. For the tolerance torch.allclose(atol=1e-2, rtol=1e-2), we need |diff| > 0.01 + 0.01*|ref|. Since the relative difference (0.5%) is strictly less than rtol (1%), the condition |diff| > rtol*|ref| can never be satisfied, and atol provides no help since absolute differences scale proportionally with outputs.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under rtol=1e-2. The ~0.5% relative change from epsilon modification is mathematically bounded below the 1% relative tolerance. No input values can overcome this fundamental limitation.
rounds.recommendations: When mutation testing epsilon parameters, use tighter tolerances (rtol < 0.005) to detect small numerical stability changes, or test with rtol=0 to require exact matches for constant-valued inputs.
